market_question: Will Renan Santos finish in second place in the first round of the 2026 Brazilian presidential election?
reasoning: Renan Santos is a co-founder of MBL and a political activist, but he lacks the national stature, party machinery, and polling support to contend for second place. The runner-up will almost certainly be a major figure from the traditional left or right. A 6.5% implied probability drastically overstates his odds; a true probability around 0.5% reflects the wide field of well-known rivals.
evidence_points: No early 2026 presidential polls feature Renan Santos among the top candidates.
Historical precedent shows second place is won by nationally recognized politicians from large parties, not minor activists.
Santos’ political movement (MBL) has limited electoral success and no major institutional backing for a presidential run.
sources_consulted: General knowledge of Brazilian political landscape
Recent surveys (e.g., Ipec, Datafolha) showing leading candidacies for 2026
